script: I discovered Toronto's coffee shops are a sham—fast‑food beats them all.. I started my day in Toronto, hunting for the next spot to chill or cram. I'd scoured Instagram, asked friends, and ended up in a bunch of cafés that bragged about latte art and "the vibe." They're usually run by kids who think coffee is a craft project. They open at 9 a.male., close at 5 p.male., and serve a watery mix of beans and milk that feels like it could be a school science experiment. I am telling you, the espresso is basically diluted coffee with a splash of dairy. Even the "premium" places are the same. If they're just a lounge with a coffee machine, they should rebrand. Honestly, none of them are worth the hype. The only place that actually mattered was that Italian shop in Montreal—Olympico. The coffee there was solid, like real, not some Instagram filter. Every day, the McDonald's brew is my go-to. It's surprisingly good, even with just a splash of cream or a spoonful of sugar. Maybe my taste buds are messed up, or maybe I am just the one who's wrong. Either way, I am sticking with the fast‑food drip. (I know, right?)
